proofs.proof_tex:
By \(\text{ass:strict-decrease}\), the three matrices \(H_j\) are positive definite, so every square root and inverse used below exists.  Put
\[
 U=H_1^{-1/2}WH_0^{1/2}.
\]
The first covariance equation in \(\text{def:raw-fiber}\) is equivalent to
\[
 UU^{\mathsf T}
 =H_1^{-1/2}WH_0W^{\mathsf T}H_1^{-1/2}=I_p.
\]
Since \(U\) is square, this says exactly that \(U\in O(p)\), and the inverse change of variables is \(W=H_1^{1/2}UH_0^{-1/2}\).  Under this change of variables, the second covariance equation is
\[
 H_1^{1/2}URU^{\mathsf T}H_1^{1/2}=H_2,
 \qquad\text{or equivalently}\qquad URU^{\mathsf T}=S.
\]
Thus \(SU=UR\).  Because \(R\) and \(S\) are real symmetric positive-definite matrices, an orthogonal intertwiner exists only if their eigenvalues, including multiplicities, agree.  If they agree, their spectral resolutions give
\[
 U=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}Q_\lambda O_\lambda P_\lambda^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad O_\lambda\in O(m_\lambda),
\]
and this representation is unique relative to the fixed orthonormal frames \(P_\lambda,Q_\lambda\): indeed, \(SU=UR\) maps the \(\lambda\)-eigenspace of \(R\) into the \(\lambda\)-eigenspace of \(S\), and \(O_\lambda=Q_\lambda^{\mathsf T}UP_\lambda\).

The two mean equations become, after multiplication by \(H_1^{-1/2}\),
\[
 U H_0^{-1/2}[d_0,d_1]=H_1^{-1/2}[d_1,d_2].
\]
Projecting this equality onto the \(\lambda\)-eigenspace of \(S\) gives precisely
\[
 O_\lambda A_\lambda=B_\lambda.
\]
Necessity of the block Gram condition follows from orthogonality:
\[
 B_\lambda^{\mathsf T}B_\lambda
 =A_\lambda^{\mathsf T}O_\lambda^{\mathsf T}O_\lambda A_\lambda
 =A_\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_\lambda.
\]

Conversely, suppose the spectra match and the displayed Gram equality holds in every block.  For a fixed \(\lambda\), define on \(\operatorname{ran}(A_\lambda)\)
\[
 L_\lambda(A_\lambda c)=B_\lambda c,
 \qquad c\in\mathbb R^2.
\]
This is well defined: if \(A_\lambda c=0\), then
\[
 \lVert B_\lambda c\rVert^2
 =c^{\mathsf T}B_\lambda^{\mathsf T}B_\lambda c
 =c^{\mathsf T}A_\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_\lambda c=0.
\]
The same Gram identity shows that \(L_\lambda\) preserves all inner products and maps onto \(\operatorname{ran}(B_\lambda)\).  In particular the two ranges have the common dimension \(r_\lambda\).  Choose orthonormal frames \(F_A,F_B\) for these ranges and frames \(N_A,N_B\) for their orthogonal complements, arranging \(F_B^{\mathsf T}L_\lambda F_A=I_{r_\lambda}\).  Every orthogonal extension, and no other one, is
\[
 O_\lambda=F_BF_A^{\mathsf T}+N_B Z_\lambda N_A^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad Z_\lambda\in O(k_\lambda).
\]
It satisfies \(O_\lambda A_\lambda=B_\lambda\).  Hence the choices form a torsor for \(O(k_\lambda)\), including the conventions that \(O(0)\) is trivial and \(O(1)=\{-1,1\}\).  Since \(\dim O(k)=k(k-1)/2\), substitution into the inverse whitening map yields exactly, without repetition,
\[
 W=H_1^{1/2}\left(\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}Q_\lambda O_\lambda P_\lambda^{\mathsf T}\right)H_0^{-1/2}.
\]
This proves both directions of the certificate and the asserted fiber dimensions.

First derive the observable restrictions from the structural model.  By \(\text{ass:linear-flow}\), \(\text{ass:initial-gaussian}\), \(\text{ass:common-measurement-noise}\), \(\text{ass:measurement-independence}\), and \(\text{ass:no-process-noise}\),
\[
 m_k=V^k(\mu_0-x^\star)+x^\star,
 \qquad
 C_k=V^k\Sigma(V^{\mathsf T})^k+E.
\]
Consequently the common noise cancels from adjacent differences and
\[
 H_j=V^j(\Sigma-V\Sigma V^{\mathsf T})(V^{\mathsf T})^j,
 \qquad
 d_j=V^j(V-I_p)(\mu_0-x^\star).
\]
It follows equation by equation that
\[
 VH_0V^{\mathsf T}=H_1,\quad VH_1V^{\mathsf T}=H_2,
 \quad Vd_0=d_1,\quad Vd_1=d_2,
\]
so every explanation supplies a raw candidate.

Necessity of the filters follows next.  A complex Schur triangularization of \(G\) makes \(\exp(hG)\) triangular with diagonal entries \(e^{hg}\), where \(g\) ranges over the eigenvalues of \(G\).  Thus \(\text{ass:hurwitz}\) gives \(\rho(V)<1\).  Moreover \(e^{hg}\) cannot lie on \(( -\infty,0]\): it is nonzero, and a negative real value would require \(\operatorname{Im}(hg)\equiv\pi\pmod {2\pi}\), contrary to \(\text{ass:alias-strip}\).  Finally,
\[
 \Sigma-V\Sigma V^{\mathsf T}=H_0,
\]
so uniqueness of the stable Stein solve gives \(T_V=\Sigma\), and then \(E_V=C_0-T_V=E\succ0\).

For sufficiency, fix \(W\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{adm}}\).  Since \(\rho(W)<1\), the series
\[
 T_W=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}W^jH_0(W^{\mathsf T})^j
\]
converges in every matrix norm and satisfies \(T_W-WT_WW^{\mathsf T}=H_0\).  It is positive definite because its first summand is \(H_0\succ0\).  It is unique: vectorization turns the homogeneous Stein equation into
\[
 (I_{p^2}-W\otimes W)\operatorname{vec}(T)=0,
\]
and every eigenvalue of \(W\otimes W\) is a product of two eigenvalues of \(W\), hence has modulus less than one.  Set \(E_W=C_0-T_W\), which is positive definite by membership in \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{adm}}\).  The Stein identity gives
\[
 WT_WW^{\mathsf T}+E_W=T_W-H_0+C_0=C_1.
\]
If \(\widetilde C_k=W^kT_W(W^{\mathsf T})^k+E_W\), then
\[
 \widetilde C_k-\widetilde C_{k+1}=W^kH_0(W^{\mathsf T})^k.
\]
The two raw congruences identify the right side successively with \(H_0,H_1,H_2\).  Since \(\widetilde C_0=C_0\), telescoping therefore yields \(\widetilde C_k=C_k\) for \(k=0,1,2,3\).

Stability implies \(I_p-W\) is invertible.  Put
\[
 x_W^\star=(I_p-W)^{-1}(m_1-Wm_0),\qquad \widetilde m_0=m_0,
 \qquad \widetilde m_{k+1}=W\widetilde m_k+(I_p-W)x_W^\star.
\]
Then \(\widetilde m_1=m_1\).  Moreover the increments obey
\[
 \widetilde m_{k+1}-\widetilde m_k=W(\widetilde m_k-\widetilde m_{k-1}).
\]
The raw equations \(Wd_0=d_1\) and \(Wd_1=d_2\) consequently imply, successively, \(\widetilde m_2=m_2\) and \(\widetilde m_3=m_3\).  Thus the reconstructed initial mean is necessarily \(\mu_0=m_0\).

It remains to justify the continuous-time coordinate and its uniqueness.  On the slit plane \(\mathbb C\setminus(-\infty,0]\), define \(\operatorname{Log}(W)\) by the holomorphic functional calculus.  Complex conjugation of the defining contour integral shows that it is real when \(W\) is real.  Spectral mapping gives
\[
 \operatorname{spec}(\operatorname{Log}W)
 =\{\log|w|+i\operatorname{Arg}(w):w\in\operatorname{spec}(W),\ -\pi<\operatorname{Arg}(w)<\pi\}.
\]
Hence \(G_W=h^{-1}\operatorname{Log}(W)\) is real, has spectrum in the required alias strip, and is Hurwitz because \(|w|<1\).  If another real logarithm \(L\) of \(W\) had all eigenvalues in the same open strip, then the scalar identity \(\operatorname{Log}(e^z)=z\) on that strip, composed through the holomorphic functional calculus, would give \(L=\operatorname{Log}(e^L)=\operatorname{Log}(W)\).  Thus no logarithm branch remains.

Now take \(X_0\sim\mathcal N(m_0,T_W)\), generate the deterministic affine trajectory with \((W,x_W^\star)\), and take mutually independent \(\mathcal N(0,E_W)\) measurement errors independent of \(X_0\).  The preceding identities show that every resulting marginal has exactly mean \(m_k\) and covariance \(C_k\).  Gaussian laws are determined by these two moments, so this construction reproduces all four observed laws.  Conversely, the necessity argument recovers every coordinate of any explanation from its \(W\).  Because \(\theta(W,z)\) includes \(W\) itself, the correspondence is injective as well as surjective.  The identified set is therefore exactly the image of \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{adm}}\), and global identification is equivalent to that fiber containing one element.

For three snapshots only, whiten the first covariance equation by setting
\[
 U=H_1^{-1/2}WH_0^{1/2},\qquad
 a=H_0^{-1/2}d_0,\qquad c=H_1^{-1/2}d_1.
\]
Then \(W\in\mathcal F_3\) if and only if
\[
 U\in O(p),\qquad Ua=c.
\]
At compatible data \(\lVert a\rVert=\lVert c\rVert\).  When \(d_0\ne0\), both vectors are nonzero, and after fixing one orthogonal map taking \(a/\lVert a\rVert\) to \(c/\lVert c\rVert\), all others are obtained by an arbitrary orthogonal action on the \((p-1)\)-dimensional orthogonal complement.  Thus the raw three-snapshot fiber is a torsor for \(O(p-1)\) and has dimension
\[
 \dim O(p-1)=\frac{(p-1)(p-2)}2.
\]
At an admissible explanation the stability, spectral-cut, and reconstructed-covariance inequalities are strict.  They are continuous in \(W\), while the stable Stein solution is continuous, so their intersection with the raw fiber is relatively open.  Every admissible explanation therefore has a neighborhood in the admissible fiber of the same dimension.  This dimension is positive for \(p\ge3\).

For four snapshots, the raw covariance equations and invertibility of \(W,H_0,H_1\) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 M_1W
 &=H_2H_1^{-1}W\\
 &=WH_1W^{\mathsf T}(WH_0W^{\mathsf T})^{-1}W\\
 &=WH_1H_0^{-1}=WM_0.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Together with \(d_1=Wd_0\), induction gives
\[
 M_1^jd_1=WM_0^jd_0\quad(0\le j<p),
 \qquad K_1=WK_0.
\]
Hence \(\det K_0\ne0\) yields the observable rational identity
\[
 V=K_1K_0^{-1}.
\]

To verify genericity rather than assume it, choose pairwise distinct numbers \(0<v_i<1\), let \(V=\operatorname{diag}(v_1,\ldots,v_p)\), \(\Sigma=I_p\), \(E=I_p\), and choose every coordinate of \(\mu_0-x^\star\) nonzero.  Then
\[
 H_0=\operatorname{diag}(1-v_i^2),\qquad M_0=\operatorname{diag}(v_i^2),
\]
and every coordinate of \(d_0=(V-I_p)(\mu_0-x^\star)\) is nonzero.  Therefore
\[
 \det K_0=\left(\prod_{i=1}^p d_{0i}\right)
 \prod_{1\le i<j\le p}(v_j^2-v_i^2)\ne0.
\]
This example satisfies all strict-decrease and admissibility inequalities.  In general \(\det K_0\) is rational in the entries of \((V,\Sigma,E,x^\star,\mu_0)\), with denominators powers of \(\det H_0\).  Clearing those nonzero denominators gives a polynomial which is not identically zero by the example.  A nonzero real polynomial has a zero set of empty interior and Lebesgue measure zero, as follows by induction on the number of coordinates and the fact that a nonzero univariate polynomial has finitely many roots.  Thus cyclicity fails only on a proper algebraic subset of the open admissible parameter domain.  Off that subset the displayed rational map uniquely recovers \(V\), and \(\text{thm:admissible-fiber}\) then uniquely recovers the full explanation whenever that candidate passes its filters.

By \(\text{thm:block-certificate}\), whenever the raw fiber is nonempty it is a product, over \(\lambda\in\Lambda\), of torsors for \(O(k_\lambda)\).  The group \(O(0)\) has one element, \(O(1)\) has two elements, and \(O(k)\) has positive dimension \(k(k-1)/2\) for \(k\ge2\).  It follows immediately that the raw fiber is finite exactly when every \(k_\lambda\le1\), and in that case its cardinality is
\[
 \prod_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\#O(k_\lambda)
 =2^{\#\{\lambda:k_\lambda=1\}}=2^q.
\]
If some \(k_\lambda\ge2\), the strict admissibility filters in \(\text{thm:admissible-fiber}\) define a relatively open subset of the raw fiber.  Hence every admissible member has a positive-dimensional local fiber.

It remains to prove attainability of the exponential count.  First take a two-dimensional block with \(0<a,b<1\):
\[
 V_{a,b}=\begin{pmatrix}0&-a\\ b&0\end{pmatrix},\quad
 \Sigma_{a,b}=\frac1{1-a^2b^2}
 \begin{pmatrix}1+a^2&0\\0&1+b^2\end{pmatrix},\quad E_{a,b}=I_2,
 \quad \mu_0=x^\star=0.
\]
Direct multiplication gives
\[
 H_0=I_2,\qquad H_1=\operatorname{diag}(a^2,b^2),\qquad
 H_2=a^2b^2I_2,
\]
so strict decrease holds.  If \(a^2\ne b^2\), the two eigenvalue blocks are one dimensional and, because every mean probe is zero, each has \(k_\lambda=1\).  The four raw completions are
\[
 W_{s,t}=\begin{pmatrix}0&sa\\tb&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad s,t\in\{-1,1\}.
\]
Their eigenvalues solve \(z^2-st\,ab=0\).  When \(st=-1\), the eigenvalues are \(\pm i\sqrt{ab}\); the two candidates are \(V_{a,b}\) and \(-V_{a,b}\), both stable and off the logarithm cut.  They have the same Stein solution \(\Sigma_{a,b}\) and recovered noise \(I_2\).  When \(st=1\), one eigenvalue is \(-\sqrt{ab}\), so the logarithm-cut filter rejects the candidate.  Thus exactly two of the four raw completions are compatible.

For \(p=2\ell\), take a direct sum of \(\ell\) such blocks, choosing all numbers \(a_j^2,b_j^2\) pairwise distinct, and take the corresponding direct sums of \(\Sigma_{a_j,b_j}\) and identity noise.  The global quotient spectrum is simple, so the raw completion signs cannot mix coordinates.  A candidate passes the cut precisely when, independently in every two-dimensional block, its two signs have opposite product.  The passing block is then \(V_{a_j,b_j}\) or \(-V_{a_j,b_j}\), so its covariance sequence, Stein solution, and positive noise are unchanged.  All blocks remain stable.  There are exactly \(2^\ell\) compatible explanations.

For \(p=2\ell+1\), append a scalar block with \(0<c<1\), \(\Sigma_c=(1-c^2)^{-1}\), \(E_c=1\), and a value of \(c^2\) distinct from every preceding squared parameter.  Its differences are \(1,c^2,c^4\), its raw completions are \(c\) and \(-c\), and only \(c\) passes the logarithm-cut filter.  Therefore the full system has exactly \(2^\ell=2^{\lfloor p/2\rfloor}\) compatible explanations.  Each passing \(W\) has a unique generator in the alias strip by \(\text{thm:admissible-fiber}\), so this is also the exact number of full structural explanations.

Let \(A\) be a perturbation of a compatible transition \(W\).  Differentiating the four components of \(F_{\mathrm{res}}\) at the exact moment vector gives
\[
 D_WF[A]=\bigl(\operatorname{vech}(AH_0W^{\mathsf T}+WH_0A^{\mathsf T}),
 \operatorname{vech}(AH_1W^{\mathsf T}+WH_1A^{\mathsf T}),Ad_0,Ad_1\bigr).
\]
Put
\[
 U=H_1^{-1/2}WH_0^{1/2}\in O(p),\qquad
 Z=H_1^{-1/2}AH_0^{1/2}.
\]
The first linearized covariance equation is \(ZU^{\mathsf T}+UZ^{\mathsf T}=0\).  Thus \(Z=UJ\) for a unique skew-symmetric matrix \(J\).  Substitution in the second equation, using \(H_1=H_0^{1/2}RH_0^{1/2}\), gives
\[
 JR+RJ^{\mathsf T}=0,
 \qquad\text{hence}\qquad JR=RJ.
\]
The two mean equations are equivalent to
\[
 JH_0^{-1/2}d_0=0,\qquad JH_0^{-1/2}d_1=0.
\]
Because \(R\) is symmetric, \(JR=RJ\) makes \(J\) block diagonal in its eigenspaces.  In the \(\lambda\)-block, the last two equations say precisely that the skew-symmetric block \(J_\lambda\) annihilates \(\operatorname{ran}(A_\lambda)\), an \(r_\lambda\)-dimensional subspace.  Relative to that subspace and its orthogonal complement,
\[
 J_\lambda=0_{r_\lambda}\oplus \widetilde J_\lambda,\qquad
 \widetilde J_\lambda^{\mathsf T}=-\widetilde J_\lambda,\qquad
 \widetilde J_\lambda\in\mathbb R^{k_\lambda\times k_\lambda}.
\]
All changes of variables above are invertible.  Since the space of skew-symmetric \(k\)-by-\(k\) matrices has dimension \(k(k-1)/2\),
\[
 \dim\ker(D_WF)=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\frac{k_\lambda(k_\lambda-1)}2.
\]

Now consider the full structural coordinates \((W,T,E,x^\star,\mu_0)\) and the map from them to the four Gaussian means and covariances.  If their moment derivative vanishes, then the derivatives of all \(H_j,d_j\) vanish, so its \(W\)-component belongs to the kernel just computed.  Conversely, fix \(A\in\ker(D_WF)\).  The derivative \(\dot T\) required to keep \(H_0=T-WTW^{\mathsf T}\) fixed is uniquely determined by
\[
 \dot T-W\dot TW^{\mathsf T}=ATW^{\mathsf T}+WTA^{\mathsf T},
\]
because the stable Stein operator is invertible.  Keeping \(C_0=T+E\) fixed then uniquely forces \(\dot E=-\dot T\).  Keeping \(m_0=\mu_0\) fixed forces \(\dot\mu_0=0\), and keeping
\[
 m_1=W\mu_0+(I_p-W)x^\star
\]
fixed uniquely forces
\[
 \dot x^\star=-(I_p-W)^{-1}A(\mu_0-x^\star).
\]
The relations \(Ad_0=Ad_1=0\) then keep \(m_2,m_3\) fixed, and the two linearized congruences keep \(C_2,C_3\) fixed.  Hence projection onto the \(W\)-coordinate is a linear bijection between the kernel of the full moment derivative and \(\ker(D_WF)\).  Replacing \(W\) by its principal-logarithm coordinate \(G_W\) is a local smooth bijection and does not alter this nullity.

Finally, for one Gaussian marginal with positive-definite covariance \(C\), a mean perturbation \(u\) and symmetric covariance perturbation \(A_C\) have Fisher quadratic form
\[
 u^{\mathsf T}C^{-1}u+\frac12\operatorname{tr}(C^{-1}A_CC^{-1}A_C).
\]
This follows by differentiating the Gaussian log density and evaluating its second moments; after writing \(A_C=C^{1/2}BC^{1/2}\), the second term is \(\frac12\operatorname{tr}(B^2)\ge0\), with equality only for \(A_C=0\).  Summing over the four independent positive-covariance marginals preserves this property.  Therefore the Fisher-information kernel equals the full moment-derivative kernel.  Its nullity is zero exactly when every \(k_\lambda\le1\), which is exactly the finite-raw-stratum condition given by the product of orthogonal completion fibers in \(\text{thm:block-certificate}\).

Use operator norm for ordinary matrices and Frobenius norm for the singular values and inverse norm of the Stein operator.  The constant \(c_T\) is understood with its corrected core formula
\[
 c_T=2\sigma_{\mathrm{Stein}}^{-1}
 \left[2\sqrt p+c_V(2\lVert V\rVert+1)\lVert T_V\rVert_F\right].
\]
Write a hat for a perturbed quantity and \(\Delta A=\widehat A-A\).  The coordinatewise hypothesis gives
\[
 \lVert\Delta H_j\rVert\le2\epsilon,\qquad
 \lVert\Delta d_j\rVert\le2\epsilon.
\]
If \(\epsilon\le a_0/4\), then for every unit vector \(u\),
\[
 u^{\mathsf T}\widehat H_i u\ge u^{\mathsf T}H_i u-\lVert\Delta H_i\rVert
 \ge a_0-2\epsilon\ge a_0/2,
\]
for \(i=0,1\), hence
\[
 \lVert\widehat H_i^{-1}\rVert\le\frac2{a_0}.
\]
The inverse identity and the definition of \(B_{\mathrm{norm}}\) then give, for \(i=0,1\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \lVert\widehat M_i-M_i\rVert
 &\le \lVert\Delta H_{i+1}\rVert\lVert\widehat H_i^{-1}\rVert
 +\lVert H_{i+1}\rVert\lVert\widehat H_i^{-1}\rVert
 \lVert\Delta H_i\rVert\lVert H_i^{-1}\rVert\\
 &\le\left(\frac4{a_0}+\frac{4B_{\mathrm{norm}}}{a_0^2}\right)\epsilon
 =c_M\epsilon.
 \end{aligned}
\]
When also \(c_M\epsilon\le1\), both \(M_i\) and \(\widehat M_i\) have norm at most \(L_M\).  The telescoping identity
\[
 \widehat M_i^j-M_i^j
 =\sum_{\ell=0}^{j-1}\widehat M_i^\ell(\widehat M_i-M_i)M_i^{j-1-\ell}
\]
therefore yields
\[
 \lVert\widehat M_i^j\widehat d_i-M_i^jd_i\rVert
 \le\left(2L_M^j+jL_M^{j-1}c_MD_{\mathrm{norm}}\right)\epsilon.
\]
The second summand is zero for \(j=0\).  Bounding matrix operator norm by Frobenius norm, column by column, proves
\[
 \lVert\widehat K_i-K_i\rVert\le c_K\epsilon,\qquad i=0,1.
\]

On the population cyclic chart, \(K_1=VK_0\) by \(\text{thm:snapshot-frontier}\).  If \(c_K\epsilon\le\kappa/2\), then \(\sigma_{\min}(\widehat K_0)\ge\kappa/2\), so \(\widehat K_0^{-1}\) exists and has norm at most \(2/\kappa\).  Hence
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}-V
 &=(\Delta K_1-V\Delta K_0)\widehat K_0^{-1},\\
 \lVert\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}-V\rVert
 &\le\frac{2c_K(1+\lVert V\rVert)}\kappa\epsilon
 =c_V\epsilon.
 \end{aligned}
\]

Suppose now \(\epsilon<\epsilon_{\mathrm{rec}}\).  Then \(c_V\epsilon<1\), and the last bound is smaller than both \(\delta_{\mathrm{stab}}/2\) and \(\delta_{\log}/2\).  By the definitions of these distances, \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}\) is stable and its spectrum avoids \(( -\infty,0]\).  For the Stein operators,
\[
 \lVert\mathcal L_{\widehat W}-\mathcal L_V\rVert_{F\to F}
 \le \lVert\widehat W-V\rVert(\lVert\widehat W\rVert+\lVert V\rVert)
 \le c_V(2\lVert V\rVert+1)\epsilon
 <\frac{\sigma_{\mathrm{Stein}}}{2}.
\]
Thus \(\mathcal L_{\widehat W}\) is invertible and
\[
 \lVert\mathcal L_{\widehat W}^{-1}\rVert_{F\to F}
 \le2\sigma_{\mathrm{Stein}}^{-1}.
\]
Subtracting the two Stein equations gives
\[
 \mathcal L_{\widehat W}(\widehat T_{\mathrm{cyc}}-T_V)
 =\Delta H_0-(\mathcal L_{\widehat W}-\mathcal L_V)T_V.
\]
Since \(\lVert\Delta H_0\rVert_F\le2\sqrt p\,\epsilon\), it follows that
\[
 \lVert\widehat T_{\mathrm{cyc}}-T_V\rVert
 \le \lVert\widehat T_{\mathrm{cyc}}-T_V\rVert_F
 \le c_T\epsilon.
\]
Consequently
\[
 \lVert\widehat E_{\mathrm{cyc}}-E_V\rVert
 \le\lVert\Delta C_0\rVert+\lVert\widehat T_{\mathrm{cyc}}-T_V\rVert
 \le(1+c_T)\epsilon=c_E\epsilon.
\]
If \(\epsilon<\epsilon_{\mathrm{adm}}\), applying the same unit-vector inequality to the reconstructed covariance errors gives
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(\widehat T_{\mathrm{cyc}})>t_{\min}/2>0,
 \qquad
 \lambda_{\min}(\widehat E_{\mathrm{cyc}})>e_{\min}/2>0.
\]

For completeness, all remaining coordinates have linear bounds on this same neighborhood.  The closed ball of radius \(\delta_{\log}/2\) about \(V\) is contained in the logarithm domain.  A contour \(\Gamma\) in the slit plane surrounding the spectra along every segment from \(V\) to such a matrix gives, by the resolvent identity,
\[
 \lVert\operatorname{Log}(\widehat W)-\operatorname{Log}(V)\rVert
 \le L_{\log}\lVert\widehat W-V\rVert,
\]
where one may take
\[
 L_{\log}=\frac{\operatorname{length}(\Gamma)}{2\pi}
 \max_{\zeta\in\Gamma}|\log\zeta|
 \sup_{U}\sup_{\zeta\in\Gamma}\lVert(\zeta I_p-U)^{-1}\rVert^2<\infty,
\]
with \(U\) ranging over those segments.  Thus the generator error is at most \(h^{-1}L_{\log}c_V\epsilon\).

Let \(\eta=\lVert(I_p-V)^{-1}\rVert\).  The distance from \(V\) to a matrix having eigenvalue one is \(\sigma_{\min}(I_p-V)=\eta^{-1}\); such matrices lie in \(\{U:\rho(U)\ge1\}\).  Hence \(\delta_{\mathrm{stab}}\le\eta^{-1}\), and the reconstruction radius implies \(\eta\lVert\widehat W-V\rVert<1/2\).  Therefore \(\lVert(I_p-\widehat W)^{-1}\rVert\le2\eta\).  Comparing the two equilibrium equations yields
\[
 \lVert\widehat x^\star-x^\star\rVert
 \le2\eta\left[2+\lVert V\rVert+c_V(\lVert m_0\rVert+\lVert x^\star\rVert)\right]\epsilon.
\]
Finally \(\lVert\widehat\mu_0-\mu_0\rVert=\lVert\widehat m_0-m_0\rVert\le\epsilon\).  This proves definedness and the asserted quantitative conclusions.  No step used the exact raw equations at the perturbed moments: those equations were used only at the population point to obtain \(K_1=VK_0\), so the final caveat also follows.

Identify a matrix \(U\) with \(u=\operatorname{vec}(U)\), write \(f(u;\zeta)=F_{\mathrm{res}}(U;\zeta)\), and let
\[
 Q(u;\zeta)=\frac12\lVert f(u;\zeta)\rVert_2^2,
 \qquad
 \Psi(u;\zeta)=D_uf(u;\zeta)^{\mathsf T}f(u;\zeta).
\]
At the fixed exact branch \((w,z)\), \(f(w;z)=0\).  Therefore
\[
 D_u\Psi(w;z)=D_uf(w;z)^{\mathsf T}D_uf(w;z).
\]
The hypothesis \(\gamma_W>0\) makes this matrix positive definite, with smallest eigenvalue \(\gamma_W^2\).  To see the local construction directly, set \(A_0=[D_u\Psi(w;z)]^{-1}\) and \(\Phi_\zeta(u)=u-A_0\Psi(u;\zeta)\).  Its derivative in \(u\) is zero at \((w,z)\).  Continuity therefore supplies neighborhoods on which \(\Phi_\zeta\) is a contraction and maps a closed ball about \(w\) into itself.  Iteration is Cauchy at a geometric rate, so it has a unique fixed point \(u(\zeta)\) there; this fixed point is the unique local stationary point.  Continuity of the Hessian keeps it positive definite, so the point is the unique local minimizer defining \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{loc}}\).  Subtracting the two fixed-point equations and applying a first-order Taylor expansion proves differentiability, and repeated differentiation proves smoothness.  Its first derivative is
\[
 Du(z)[a]=-\bigl(D_WF^{\mathsf T}D_WF\bigr)^{-1}
 D_WF^{\mathsf T}D_zF[a].
\]
The isolating-ball hypothesis selects this branch and excludes every other population root from the local construction.

Strict stability, logarithm-cut, Stein, covariance-positivity, and equilibrium margins make every operation in \(\theta(U,\zeta)\) smooth near \((W,z)\).  In particular, the Stein derivative is obtained by solving an invertible linear equation, the logarithm derivative by its resolvent integral, and the equilibrium derivative by differentiating an inverse.  The composite branch map
\[
 g(\zeta)=\theta(U(\zeta),\zeta)
\]
is therefore smooth, and its derivative at \(z\) is exactly \(J_\theta\).

It remains to establish the moment limit used by the theorem.  For one snapshot, write \(Y=m+Z\) with \(Z\sim\mathcal N(0,C)\), and define the centered single-observation moment vector
\[
 \xi=\bigl(Z,\operatorname{vech}(ZZ^{\mathsf T}-C)\bigr).
\]
It has finite moments of every order.  Differentiating the Gaussian moment-generating function \(\exp(t^{\mathsf T}Ct/2)\) shows
\[
 \mathbb E[Z_iZ_jZ_\ell]=0,\qquad
 \operatorname{Cov}(Z_iZ_j,Z_rZ_s)=C_{ir}C_{js}+C_{is}C_{jr}.
\]
Thus the mean and covariance blocks of \(\operatorname{Cov}(\xi)\) have zero cross-covariance.  More explicitly, if \(L_p\) is the elimination matrix satisfying \(\operatorname{vech}(A)=L_p\operatorname{vec}(A)\) for symmetric \(A\), and \(\mathsf K_p\operatorname{vec}(A)=\operatorname{vec}(A^{\mathsf T})\), then the contribution of snapshot \(k\) to \(\Omega\) is
\[
 \Omega_k=\frac1{\pi_k}\operatorname{diag}\!\left(
 C_k,\ L_p(I_{p^2}+\mathsf K_p)(C_k\otimes C_k)L_p^{\mathsf T}\right),
 \qquad \Omega=\operatorname{diag}(\Omega_0,\Omega_1,\Omega_2,\Omega_3).
\]
The usual sample covariance differs from the average of \(ZZ^{\mathsf T}\) by the outer product of the sample-mean error and, if the divisor is \(n-1\), an asymptotically negligible factor; this difference is \(O_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1})\).

For completeness, the finite-dimensional Gaussian limit follows from the characteristic function calculation
\[
 \mathbb E\exp\!\left(i t^{\mathsf T}\xi/\sqrt n\right)
 =1-\frac{t^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{Cov}(\xi)t}{2n}+o(n^{-1}),
\]
whose \(n\)-th power tends to \(\exp[-t^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{Cov}(\xi)t/2]\).  Applying this at each independent snapshot and using \(n_k/N\to\pi_k\in(0,1)\) gives
\[
 \sqrt N(\widehat z-z)\Longrightarrow\mathcal N(0,\Omega).
\]
The blocks from different snapshot labels are independent; all correlations created later by forming \(H_j,d_j\) are retained because these differences are fixed linear transformations of the full vector \(z\).

Taylor expansion of the smooth map \(g\) gives
\[
 \sqrt N\{g(\widehat z)-g(z)\}
 =J_\theta\sqrt N(\widehat z-z)+o_{\mathbb P}(1),
\]
and substitution of the preceding characteristic-function limit proves
\[
 \sqrt N\bigl(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{loc}}-\theta(W,z)\bigr)
 \Longrightarrow\mathcal N(0,J_\theta\Omega J_\theta^{\mathsf T}).
\]
In particular the last coordinate is \(\widehat\mu_0=\widehat m_0\).  The empirical covariances converge to \(C_k\), the deterministic shares converge to \(\pi_k\), and the smooth local solution converges to \(W\).  The explicit Gaussian fourth-moment formula above and continuity of all derivatives therefore imply that replacing \((z,W,\Omega,J_\theta)\) by their empirical plug-in counterparts converges in probability to \(J_\theta\Omega J_\theta^{\mathsf T}\).  This establishes consistent covariance estimation separately on every specified regular branch, without requiring empirical spectral or Gram equalities.

proposed.name: c_T
proposed.def: Stein-reconstruction perturbation constant \(c_T=2\sigma_{\mathrm{Stein}}^{-1}[2\sqrt p+c_V(2\lVert V\rVert+1)\lVert T_V\rVert_F]\).
proposed.role: Linear perturbation constant for the reconstructed latent covariance.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Covariance inputs are controlled in operator norm while the Stein singular value is induced by Frobenius norm. Thus \(\lVert\Delta H_0\rVert_F\le 2\sqrt p\,\epsilon\), and the original constant without \(\sqrt p\) does not prove the stated bound. The corrected formula is exactly the constant obtained from the Neumann bound for the perturbed Stein inverse.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct an explicit output-sensitive algorithm which, from perturbed moments rather than exact spectral and Gram equalities, finds every regular noncyclic empirical branch, certifies completeness and admissibility exactly once, and assigns canonical labels with a computable positive separation radius and simultaneous coverage control.
open_obligations.obstruction: The certification handle specifies root certification only after approximate roots and an eliminated zero-dimensional system have been supplied. It contains neither a globally complete root-isolation procedure nor a quantitative lower bound separating all raw roots and all excluded roots from stability, logarithm-cut, Stein, and covariance-positivity boundaries. Regularity \(\gamma_W>0\) is local and does not provide those global margins; an excluded branch may lie on an admissibility boundary, so the requested model-count stability cannot hold uniformly on every stated regular finite stratum without an additional separation regime or a boundary-aware set-valued rule.
open_obligations.attempted: The block sign enumeration was used as a population initializer, and the residual score was linearized at each enumerated branch. This proves a smooth local estimator whenever an isolating neighborhood is already known, but applying exact eigenspace or probe-Gram tests to empirical moments fails almost surely, while local contraction and Smale-style certification certify only roots already targeted and do not establish exhaustion of all roots or a positive distance to excluded branches.
open_obligations.partial_result: The frozen results already give a complete population enumeration on every finite stratum: \(\text{thm:block-certificate}\) produces the \(2^q\) raw sign completions, \(\text{thm:admissible-fiber}\) filters them exactly, and \(\text{thm:branchwise-inference}\) gives a unique smooth residual estimator in a sufficiently small neighborhood of each regular branch.  For any fixed population instance whose raw branches are mutually separated and whose excluded branches are also separated strictly from every stability, logarithm-cut, and covariance-positivity boundary, compactness of the finite list gives a positive but presently implicit minimum of those separations.  What is not supplied is a data-based, output-sensitive procedure that finds and certifies every empirical neighborhood and computes a valid lower bound for this minimum uniformly over all regular noncyclic finite strata.

proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathcal C_4(E)\) denote the set of transition matrices that occur in a structural explanation of the four observed marginal laws with the supplied measurement covariance \(E\), under \(\text{ass:linear-flow}\), \(\text{ass:initial-gaussian}\), \(\text{ass:common-measurement-noise}\), \(\text{ass:measurement-independence}\), \(\text{ass:no-process-noise}\), \(\text{ass:hurwitz}\), \(\text{ass:alias-strip}\), and \(\text{ass:spacing}\).  This is only proof notation; it does not define the identifying functional.  We prove both inclusions
\[
\mathcal C_4(E)=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{known}}(E).
\]

First take \(W\in\mathcal C_4(E)\).  Write
\[
L_k=\operatorname{Cov}(X_k).
\]
By \(\text{ass:linear-flow}\), \(\text{ass:no-process-noise}\), and \(\text{ass:initial-gaussian}\),
\[
\mathbb E[X_k]=W^k(\mu_0-x^\star)+x^\star,
\qquad
L_k=W^k\Sigma(W^{\mathsf T})^k.
\]
The matrix \(W=\exp(hG)\) is invertible.  Hence \(\Sigma\succ0\) implies \(L_k\succ0\) for every \(k\in K\).  By the zero error means in \(\text{ass:common-measurement-noise}\) and the independence in \(\text{ass:measurement-independence}\),
\[
m_k=\mathbb E[X_k],
\qquad
C_k=L_k+E.
\]
It follows, using the supplied value of \(E\), that
\[
\widetilde C_k=C_k-E=L_k\succ0,
\qquad
W\widetilde C_kW^{\mathsf T}=\widetilde C_{k+1}\qquad(k=0,1,2).
\]
Furthermore,
\[
d_k=m_{k+1}-m_k
=W^k(W-I_p)(\mu_0-x^\star),
\]
so
\[
Wd_0=d_1,
\qquad
Wd_1=d_2.
\]

We next verify the dynamical and reconstruction restrictions in \(\text{def:known-noise-fiber}\).  Put a complex Jordan block of \(hG\) in the form \(gI+N\), where \(N\) is nilpotent.  Its exponential has sole eigenvalue \(e^g\).  Thus the spectral mapping calculation block by block gives
\[
\rho(W)=\max_{g\in\operatorname{spec}(G)}e^{h\operatorname{Re}(g)}<1
\]
by \(\text{ass:hurwitz}\).  By \(\text{ass:alias-strip}\), \(-\pi<h\operatorname{Im}(g)<\pi\); consequently no eigenvalue \(e^{hg}\) is on \(( -\infty,0]\), and therefore
\[
\operatorname{spec}(W)\cap(-\infty,0]=\varnothing.
\]
Cancellation of the common \(E\) gives
\[
H_0=C_0-C_1=L_0-L_1=L_0-WL_0W^{\mathsf T}.
\]
If \(D-WDW^{\mathsf T}=0\), vectorization yields
\[
\bigl(I_{p^2}-W\otimes W\bigr)\operatorname{vec}(D)=0.
\]
Since \(\rho(W\otimes W)=\rho(W)^2<1\), the matrix \(I_{p^2}-W\otimes W\) is invertible.  Hence the Stein equation has at most one solution.  Since \(L_0\) is a solution, the object in the frozen definition satisfies
\[
T_W=L_0=\widetilde C_0,
\qquad
E_W=C_0-T_W=C_0-\widetilde C_0=E.
\]
All conditions in \(\text{def:known-noise-fiber}\) hold, proving
\(
\mathcal C_4(E)\subseteq\mathcal F_{\mathrm{known}}(E)
\).

Conversely, let \(W\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{known}}(E)\).  Define
\[
\Sigma=\widetilde C_0,
\qquad
\mu_0=m_0,
\qquad
b=m_1-Wm_0.
\]
Membership in \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{known}}(E)\) gives \(\Sigma\succ0\) and \(\rho(W)<1\).  In particular, \(1\notin\operatorname{spec}(W)\), so division by \(I_p-W\) is valid and we may set
\[
x^\star=(I_p-W)^{-1}b.
\]
Then \(b=(I_p-W)x^\star\).  Starting from \(m_0\), the affine recursion with transition \(W\) gives
\[
Wm_0+b=m_1,
\]
and the two probe restrictions in \(\text{def:known-noise-fiber}\) give, successively,
\[
Wm_1+b
=m_1+W(m_1-m_0)
=m_1+Wd_0
=m_1+d_1
=m_2,
\]
and
\[
Wm_2+b
=m_2+W(m_2-m_1)
=m_2+Wd_1
=m_2+d_2
=m_3.
\]

It remains to exhibit the continuous-time generator required by the structural model.  Because \(W\) is real and \(\operatorname{spec}(W)\cap(-\infty,0]=\varnothing\), its principal logarithm may be seen directly in complex Jordan coordinates.  On a block \(\lambda I+N\) of size \(s\), with \(N^s=0\), it is
\[
\ell(\lambda)I+
\sum_{r=1}^{s-1}\frac{(-1)^{r+1}}{r}\left(\frac{N}{\lambda}\right)^r,
\qquad
-\pi<\operatorname{Im}\ell(\lambda)<\pi,
\]
where \(\ell\) is the scalar principal logarithm.  The finite nilpotent power-series identities \(\exp(\log(I+N/\lambda))=I+N/\lambda\) show blockwise that its exponential is \(W\).  Conjugate Jordan blocks have conjugate displayed logarithms, so their real canonical pairing shows that \(\operatorname{Log}(W)\) is real.  Its eigenvalues are \(\ell(\lambda)\).  Therefore, with \(h>0\) from \(\text{ass:spacing}\),
\[
G=h^{-1}\operatorname{Log}(W)
\]
is real and satisfies
\[
\exp(hG)=W,
\qquad
\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{spec}(G)
=h^{-1}\log|\operatorname{spec}(W)|<0,
\qquad
-\frac{\pi}{h}<\operatorname{Im}\operatorname{spec}(G)<\frac{\pi}{h}.
\]
Thus \(G\) satisfies \(\text{ass:hurwitz}\) and \(\text{ass:alias-strip}\).  The same Jordan-block calculation also shows that an original generator satisfying the open alias strip obeys \(\operatorname{Log}(\exp(hG))=hG\), so this reconstruction neither adds nor removes a permitted generator branch.

Construct \(X_0\sim\mathcal N(m_0,\Sigma)\), set
\[
X_k=W^k(X_0-x^\star)+x^\star,
\]
and take mutually independent \(\varepsilon_k\sim\mathcal N(0,E)\), independent of \(X_0\).  This construction satisfies the three distributional assumptions and has no process innovations.  The preceding mean recursion gives \(\mathbb E[X_k]=m_k\).  The level congruences in \(\text{def:known-noise-fiber}\) imply inductively that
\[
\operatorname{Cov}(X_k)
=W^k\Sigma(W^{\mathsf T})^k
=\widetilde C_k
\quad(k\in K).
\]
Consequently
\[
\mathbb E[X_k+\varepsilon_k]=m_k,
\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}(X_k+\varepsilon_k)=\widetilde C_k+E=C_k.
\]
Both sides are nonsingular Gaussian laws, so equality of their means and covariances is equality of the observed marginal laws.  Hence \(W\in\mathcal C_4(E)\), proving the reverse inclusion.  Notice also that \(E_W=E\succ0\), so the equality in the supplied-noise fiber implies the usual positivity inequality; it is strictly stronger because it fixes the nuisance to its supplied value.

For snapshots \(0,1,2\), the preceding calculation leaves exactly the two covariance transition equations
\[
W\widetilde C_0W^{\mathsf T}=\widetilde C_1,
\qquad
W\widetilde C_1W^{\mathsf T}=\widetilde C_2,
\]
and subtraction of the two affine mean recursions leaves exactly
\[
Wd_0=d_1.
\]
These are exactly the consecutive-snapshot equations in AaltoLamolineGoncalves2022, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.1, after the known measurement covariance is subtracted as prescribed in the paragraph following their Remark 2.2.  This comparison is attribution only; the advertised finite-sign reduction follows directly as follows.  Put
\[
R_0=\widetilde C_0^{-1/2}\widetilde C_1\widetilde C_0^{-1/2},
\qquad
R_1=\widetilde C_1^{-1/2}\widetilde C_2\widetilde C_1^{-1/2},
\qquad
U=\widetilde C_1^{-1/2}W\widetilde C_0^{1/2}.
\]
The first congruence is equivalent to \(UU^{\mathsf T}=I_p\), and the second is equivalent to
\[
UR_0U^{\mathsf T}=R_1.
\]
Assume precisely that the two positive-definite matrices have the same simple ordered spectrum and write
\[
R_0=P\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_p)P^{\mathsf T},
\qquad
R_1=Q\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_p)Q^{\mathsf T},
\]
with \(\lambda_i\ne\lambda_j\) for \(i\ne j\).  Then \(D=Q^{\mathsf T}UP\) is orthogonal and commutes with the diagonal matrix of distinct eigenvalues.  Entrywise,
\[
(\lambda_j-\lambda_i)D_{ij}=0,
\]
so \(D\) is diagonal; orthogonality gives \(D_{ii}\in\{-1,1\}\).  Thus all covariance-compatible transitions are among the finite list
\[
W_D=\widetilde C_1^{1/2}QD P^{\mathsf T}\widetilde C_0^{-1/2},
\qquad
D=\operatorname{diag}(s_1,\ldots,s_p),\quad s_i\in\{-1,1\}.
\]
Finally define the observable probe coordinates
\[
a=P^{\mathsf T}\widetilde C_0^{-1/2}d_0,
\qquad
c=Q^{\mathsf T}\widetilde C_1^{-1/2}d_1.
\]
The mean equation is equivalent to \(Da=c\).  If every \(a_i\ne0\), each possible sign is computably fixed by
\[
s_i=\frac{c_i}{a_i},
\]
and compatibility requires this ratio to lie in \(\{-1,1\}\).  Thus the three-snapshot known-\(E\) system reduces to a finite enumeration of at most \(2^p\) sign patterns, followed by the explicit probe test, as claimed.

proposed.statement: Suppose the common measurement covariance \(E\) is supplied and set \(\widetilde C_k=C_k-E\). The transition fiber compatible with the four observed levels is exactly \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{known}}(E)\): its covariance restrictions are the level congruences \(W\widetilde C_kW^{\mathsf T}=\widetilde C_{k+1}\) for \(k=0,1,2\), and its reconstructed residual-noise restriction is the equality \(E_W=E\), equivalently \(C_0-E-T_W=0\), rather than the unknown-noise inequality \(C_0-T_W\succ0\). Restriction to snapshots \(k=0,1,2\) gives exactly the two level-covariance congruences \(W\widetilde C_0W^{\mathsf T}=\widetilde C_1\) and \(W\widetilde C_1W^{\mathsf T}=\widetilde C_2\), together with the affine-mean restriction \(Wd_0=d_1\), used in AaltoLamolineGoncalves2022, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.1. Under its simple generalized spectra and nonzero probe coordinates, this three-snapshot known-\(E\) system reduces to finite sign recovery.
proposed.justification: A precise reduction guards the new observation-noise regime against becoming a disconnected analogue of the published model.
proposed.gap: This is a sanity reduction to AaltoLamolineGoncalves2022 rather than an independent novelty claim.
proposed.consumer: Readers can reuse existing known-noise identification results whenever a calibration experiment supplies \(E\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The existing dependency metadata omitted the positive-spacing, Hurwitz, principal-alias-strip, measurement-independence, and no-process-innovation conditions used to prove exact structural compatibility.  The Aalto comparison is source attribution only, and the finite-sign reduction is derived directly in the proof.  The formal claim is unchanged.
